149. **Project To-Do lists: kind 44248 allocated, modelled as append-only
     field ops folded client-side, not as a NIP-33 head (2026-09-17, Andy
     with Opus).** Built on `feat/project-todo-list`; the contract is
     `docs/nips/NIP-TD.md` and `conformance/project-todo-fold/CONTRACT.md`.

     **Allocation.** 44248 is the lowest unused and unreserved kind: 44231–
     44239 are the continuity research's, 44240 Pulse with 44241–44243
     reserved, 44244–44247 the team transaction, policy, observation and
     handover. `git grep 44248` over this tree matched nothing before the
     constant existed; `git grep 44248 vanilla/main` (`12201c49b`) matched
     only hashes inside `uv.lock` files. Doc comment on
     `KIND_PROJECT_TODO_OP` in `crates/buzz-core/src/kind.rs`.

     **Why not NIP-33.** A shared list has many writers and replacement keys
     on `(kind, pubkey, d)` — one head per author
     (`crates/buzz-db/src/parameterized_event.rs:22-26`, item 113's hazard).
     The 30624 cross-author conditional path would cost a transaction lock and
     a conflict response per tick. So: one regular kind, scoped to the project
     by the canonical `a` coordinate exactly as 44240 is, each op setting
     **one field** (`list.create|title|archived`, `item.add|text|done|
     assignee|due|rank|remove`), folded by earliest-create / latest-`(created_at,
     id)`-per-field / terminal-remove rules pinned in
     `conformance/project-todo-fold/fixtures/fold-vectors.json`, which the
     Rust (`buzz-core`, used by `bee todos`), TypeScript (Desktop) and Dart
     (Mobile) folds all bind to. Order is a fractional-indexing `rank`
     (`crates/buzz-core/src/fractional_rank.rs`; `rank-vectors.json`) so a
     drag or `bee todos move --index N` is one `item.rank` op that never
     rewrites neighbours.

     **Relay.** Every chokepoint that special-cased 44240 now keys on
     `buzz_core::kind::is_project_a_scoped_kind` (ingest admission via
     `admit_project_scoped_write`, `event_visible_to_reader`, live fan-out,
     the SQL pushdown, the bridge request-shape rule), so both kinds share one
     gate: private project → owner/collaborator write, viewer read-only;
     public → any member; unknown coordinate refused; refusal is 403 (CLI
     exit 3); an `h` tag is rejected and the kind is global-only. No
     migration. `e2e_project_todos.rs`: six of seven pass against a local
     relay; the two-host cross-community case fails identically for
     `e2e_pulse.rs` on this machine (no second community configured), a test
     environment limit, not a regression.

     **Inherited limitation, recorded not fixed.** Deleting or purging a
     project's 30621 head drops its ACL row, after which the coordinate is in
     nobody's hidden set and the ops — like Pulse entries — become readable
     to community members; `project_purge.rs` never touches channel-less
     `a`-tagged events. Fix options: fail closed in the read gate when the
     coordinate has no live head (needs a DB fact the pure predicate lacks),
     or extend purge to `kind IN (44240, 44248) AND tags @> [["a", coord]]`.

     **Cold read.** A reader replays the whole op log (relay page cap 1000).
     Desktop pages by `until` and discloses `truncated` after ten full pages;
     `bee todos` uses `query_all`. A compaction record is a follow-up.

     **Verified live 2026-09-17** on a local relay on :3010 with two keys:
     `bee todos` viewer refusal exit 3, promotion, collaborator
     `done`/`move`/`assign` folding into the owner's `show`
     (`crates/buzz-cli/TESTING.md` § 6.13a); the Desktop tab against the same
     relay (`desktop/tests/e2e/project-todos.live.spec.ts`, 9 s): UI writes
     read back by the CLI, a collaborator's `add --index 0 --due` and `done`
     appearing live in the tab, a UI tick reaching the CLI fold.

     **Mobile** (`mobile/lib/features/project_todos/`, built by a delegated
     lane, gates re-run by Andy's session: `flutter analyze` clean,
     `flutter test` 2086 passed) binds the same vectors and reaches the page
     from the project tree's "To-do" row. Two disclosed gaps: no simulator
     run yet, widget tests only; and mobile has no kind-39010 roster consumer,
     so a viewer is not shown a read-only state — the controls render and the
     relay's refusal is shown verbatim in a SnackBar, never a control that
     pretends to have worked. The lane also reported, **unverified by this
     session**, that under Riverpod 3.1 `stateOrNull` is `null` inside a
     `Notifier.build()` rebuild, so the `(stateOrNull ?? initial).copyWith`
     idiom in `projects_provider.dart:84,91`, `terminals_index_provider.dart:
     105,112` and `shell_observer_provider.dart:215-226` would reset those
     pages to their initial state on a socket-status change; the to-do
     notifier keeps its read in instance fields instead. Worth a test before
     it is treated as a finding.

     **Revised the same day (2026-09-17, Andy's call): personal vs project
     lists, and shared pins.** A list is `project` (every member) or
     `personal` (its author only), fixed by `list.create` and repeated on
     every op as the `td-vis` tag so the relay withholds a personal op from
     everyone but its author on every read surface and in fan-out without
     parsing content (`buzz_core::kind::is_personal_todo_op`, wired into
     `project_a_scoped_event_hidden_from`, the fan-out branch and the SQL
     pushdown). Relay-enforced, not encrypted — the same standing as a
     private project. `list.pinned` (per-field LWW) puts a list in every
     member's project sidebar; Desktop reads pinned lists for the sidebar
     through one index hook sharing the tab's cache, the project `+` menu
     reads New coding session · New terminal · New to-do list, a rule, New
     channel · New forum, and its "New to-do list" asks Project/Personal.
     The v1 contract was revised in place because nothing had landed on
     hive; ops without `td-vis` are ignored and disclosed by the `ignored`
     counter (the dev relay on :3010 showed `ignored: 8` for the morning's
     ops). Verified live: `bee todos lists` as the collaborator never sees
     the owner's personal list; the collaborator's `pin` shows for the
     owner; the Desktop live gate covers the menu order, a personal list
     created from the sidebar appearing as a locked pinned row, and a pin
     arriving live. Mobile (delegated lane, gates re-run: 2100 tests) mirrors
     it with pinned rows under the project tree's To-do row.

     **Landed on `main` at `0cbfcf296` (2026-09-17), fast-forward, 14
     signed commits; the mobile gap above closed the same afternoon.** The
     page was exercised on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) paired to
     the Desktop dev identity against the :3010 relay: personal and project
     lists, pins under the tree's To-do row, reorder. Three things the
     simulator run turned up, fixed in the follow-up commit: (a) a phone that
     confirmed the SAS while the desktop's code had expired sat on
     "Confirmed — waiting for desktop" with no way out short of the session
     timeout — `PairingNotifier.cancelPairing()` and a Cancel button under
     the spinner (`mobile/lib/features/pairing/pairing_page.dart`, widget
     test "waiting for the desktop can be cancelled"); (b) Xcode 27 hard-
     errors any pod with a deployment target under 15.0, so `Podfile`'s
     `post_install` floors every pod at 16.0; (c) Xcode 27 has no
     `Simulator.app` — Device Hub replaces it — so `just mobile-dev` now
     accepts either host. Not ours to fix: on the iOS 27.0 runtime the
     device pasteboard is dead (`simctl pbcopy` succeeds, `pbpaste` reads
     back empty, no `com.apple.pboard` job), so the app's Paste finds
     nothing; iOS 26.5 on the same Xcode works. Known upstream
     (AndrewKochulab/sim-mirror#27; Apple forums thread 820393 for the
     Xcode 26.4 predecessor, FB22336496). Test on a 26.5 device until Apple
     fixes it.

150. **Project actions C1 built: WF-08 closed, `run_on_host`, host-step kinds 46013/46014/46022/46023, `workflow_host_steps`, provider execution, `bee actions`, Actions tab (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.4–5.6, § 7 C1 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). What is built, with the code that proves it:
   - **WF-08 is closed.** A `request_approval` step now parks the run instead of failing it: the step loop calls `suspend::persist_and_publish`, which writes the approval row, flips the run to `waiting_approval` with its full trace, and only then publishes the relay-signed 46010 (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/suspend.rs` `persist_and_publish`; `executor.rs` `StepResult::Suspended` arm). `finalize_run` logs a suspended result and writes nothing (`lib.rs` `finalize_run`), because writing again would race the grant the request invites. Ordering is the contract: row → status → publish. Proved end to end against Postgres by `suspensions_are_durable_before_they_are_announced` (`lib.rs` tests, `#[ignore = "requires Postgres"]`, run 2026-09-17 on the local dev DB: 1 passed): authored gate → `waiting_approval` with its row; grant → resume at 1 → synthetic gate bound to index 1 naming the owner; grant → resume at 1 → `waiting_host` with the host-step row and a 46013 whose `definitionHash` equals the stored hash.
   - **`run_on_host` gates itself.** The executor's `RunOnHost` arm looks for a granted approval bound to the step's own id; absent, it suspends with a synthetic approval whose `step_index` is the host step's index and whose `approver_spec` is the workflow owner's hex key (`executor.rs` `RunOnHost` arm). The relay resumes **at** that index, not after it (`suspend::resume_index_after_approval`), which is how the same approvals table serves both authored gates and the spec's synthetic one. A granted step suspends again as `waiting_host` (new `run_status` value) after `create_host_step` and the 46013 publish.
   - **The request carries no command text** (`crates/buzz-core/src/host_step.rs` `HostStepRequested`, `deny_unknown_fields`; `request_refuses_command_text_and_bad_hash` test). The host recompiles the entry from its own `beekeeper/actions.yml` (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/actions_file.rs` `parse_actions_yml`) and compares `definition_hash_hex` with the request (`hash.rs`, one function shared with the relay's `handle_workflow_def`); drift refuses `ACTION_DEFINITION_DRIFT` before any claim.
   - **Exactly one host executes.** `claim_host_step` is one `UPDATE … WHERE claimed_by IS NULL … RETURNING`; the loser is answered `AlreadyClaimed(row)` and its ingest response says `claimed by <hex>`; a result from any key but the claimant touches no row (`crates/buzz-db/src/workflow.rs` `claim_host_step`, `record_host_step_result`; Postgres-backed test `host_step_claim_is_won_exactly_once`, run 2026-09-17 against the local dev DB after `buzz-admin migrate` took it to 0043: 1 passed).
   - **Relay.** `crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/host_steps.rs` (new): `admit` checks the row exists, the `h` tag equals the workflow's channel and the signer is a channel member; `handle_host_step_claim` (46022) also requires the claim's `requestedEventId` to match the row, answers the winner `response:{"status":"claimed"}`, a repeat by the same host as a duplicate, and any other host `claimed by <hex>`; `handle_host_step_result` (46023) stores an unclaimed refusal without touching the row, requires the reporter to hold the claim and to name the recorded claim event, publishes the relay-signed 46014 (`workflow_sink.rs` `publish_relay_event`, shared with 46010 and 46013), and `resume_workflow_after_host_step` writes the step's `completed` trace entry with `host_step_output` **before** `execute_from_step(step_index + 1)`, so a later resume reconstructs `steps_<id>_output_exit_code`. `handle_workflow_def` now requires a channel owner or admin to save a definition with host steps (the step runs a command on an operator's machine) and hashes with the shared `hash_definition_value`; `resume_workflow_after_approval` derives its index with `resume_index_after_approval`. REST `GET /workflows/{id}/runs/{run}/host-steps` (`api/workflows.rs` `run_host_steps`, `router.rs`). Ingest scope and the metrics label admit 46022/46023. Postgres-backed `claim_race_has_one_winner_and_only_the_winner_reports` (`host_steps.rs` tests; run 2026-09-17: 1 passed — after fixing its own setup, which had not created the owner's user row).
   - **Provider.** `crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_step_listener.rs`: one authenticated REQ `{"kinds":[46013],"#a":[served projects]}` (the served set is `ProjectsFile.projects`' keys, re-synced on the runtime tick), every candidate `verify()`-ed, its signer compared to the witnessed relay self and decoded with `decode_host_step_requested`, expired requests dropped. `action_steps.rs`: `verify_request` runs the § 5.6 checks in order — project recorded (`ACTION_CHECKOUT_NOT_RECORDED`, naming Project settings → This computer → Repository folder), `beekeeper/actions.yml` present and parseable, entry found by name, `ACTION_DEFINITION_DRIFT` when the recompiled hash differs, step index/id/kind agree (`ACTION_STEP_MISMATCH`), limits (`resolve_run_on_host`), `env_from_host` values present (`ACTION_HOST_ENV_MISSING`); a refusal is an unclaimed 46023 `refused`. Then `consume_operation("action-step:<run>:<step>")`, the 46022 claim published **synchronously** through `publish_event_acknowledged` so a relay `claimed by <hex>` rejection is seen and recorded as `LostClaim` (`claim_winner`), `host_command::run`, and the 46023 through the durable outbox. `host_command.rs`: exec-style spawn in its own process group, output streamed to `<state_dir>/actions/<run>/<step>/{stdout,stderr}.log` capped at `artifact_max_bytes`, UTF-8-safe tails with every `env_from_host` value scrubbed, timeout → SIGTERM then SIGKILL to the group → exit 124, working directory canonicalised and required to stay inside the checkout (symlink escapes refused), `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git status --porcelain` for `headSha`/`dirty`. `action_step_store.rs` (`action-steps.json`, versioned, `atomic_write`): `Requested → Claimed → Running{pid} → Exited → Reported`, `Refused`, `LostClaim`; `recover_action_steps_on_start` publishes `lost_on_restart` for a `Running` record whose pid is gone and never re-runs anything. One disclosed limitation: if the claim's acknowledgement times out (transport, not a relay verdict) the claim is left in the durable outbox and the host proceeds as claimed; the relay then refuses that host's 46023 if another host won, so nothing runs twice on the relay's record, but the loser did run the command locally.
   - **Desktop and CLI.** A latent bug fixed on the way: the desktop's 46030/46031 builders tagged the raw token as `t` while the relay reads the hash from `d`/`e` (`command_executor.rs` `handle_approval_grant`), so every desktop grant would have been refused "missing approval reference"; `desktop/src-tauri/src/events/workflows.rs` `approval_ref_tag` now tags `["d", approval_ref]` (tests in `commands/workflows_tests.rs`). New Tauri command `get_run_host_steps` (`commands/workflows.rs`) over the new REST path. Actions tab: `actions` in `PATH_TABS` (`projects-container/ui/ProjectPageTabs.tsx`), route `app/routes/projects.$projectId.actions.tsx`, feature `desktop/src/features/project-actions/` — `lib/useProjectActions.ts` lists 30620 definitions in the project's channels whose `project` equals the coordinate, then runs, approvals and host steps per run; `lib/actionRunLabel.ts` `describeActionRun` renders only what records prove in the § 5.8 wording (`waiting approval (since …)`, `claimed by <host>, no result yet`, `exited 1 on <host> at <sha>, dirty`, `lost on host restart`, …; 9 tests); `ui/ProjectActionRunRow.tsx` approves/denies through the existing commands and shows the "allow future runs" checkbox disabled ("coming with autorun grants"). Wire types in `shared/api/workflowTypes.ts` (`types.ts` sits at 999 lines of its 1000-line ceiling, so nothing was added there). CLI `bee actions publish --project <coord> --channel <uuid> [--file beekeeper/actions.yml]` and `bee actions status` (`crates/buzz-cli/src/commands/actions.rs`): one 30620 per entry with `d` = UUID v5 of `<project>\n<name>` under `ACTIONS_NAMESPACE`, so republishing upserts; a test proves the emitted YAML re-parses on the relay's chain to the same canonical JSON and hash the host will compute.
   - **Migration 0043** adds `waiting_host` to `run_status`, the `host_step_status` enum and `workflow_host_steps`; `schema/schema.sql` mirrors it; the table is registered in `EXPECTED_SCOPED_TABLES`/`PURGE_SCOPED_TABLES` (`crates/buzz-db/src/deletion.rs`) and fenced by the desired-state DO-loop, not by an explicit `attach_community_write_fence` call — the 0029 parity test (`migration.rs` `deletion_surface_parity_between_migration_0029_and_schema_sql`) requires schema.sql's explicit list to equal 0029's. The fresh-bootstrap path is proved by `desired_state_schema_bootstrap_progresses_beyond_fencing` (`deletion.rs`, `#[ignore]`, run 2026-09-17: 1 passed) with the table in the catalog.
   - **Adversarial review (2026-09-17) and what it changed.** Two blockers found and fixed before landing: (a) a host step inherited the provider's own environment, so `command: ["sh","-c","… $BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY …"]` in a committed `actions.yml` would have exfiltrated the provider key after one approval — `host_command.rs` now strips every variable the adapter fence covers (`agent_fence::FENCE`, `BUZZ_*` and the enumerated keys) before layering the step's env, and `prepare` refuses an `env_from_host` name the fence covers (`ACTION_HOST_ENV_FENCED`; test `env_from_host_may_not_name_the_providers_own_credentials`); (b) the relay hashes a webhook definition after injecting its secret while a host hashes the plain file entry, so every webhook-triggered host step would have been refused as drift — `WorkflowDef::validate` refuses `run_on_host` with a webhook trigger, and `TriggerDef::Manual` (spec § 5.1) exists so an action a person runs by hand has an honest trigger that fires on nothing but 46020. Also fixed: a duplicate 46023 from the claiming host re-arms the resume when the run is still `waiting_host` and the resume skips an already-written trace entry (crash between commit and resume no longer parks the run forever); provider recovery reports a `Claimed` record with no process as `lost_on_restart` and re-queues an `Exited` result that was never enqueued; a claim whose acknowledgement never arrives is retried three times and then refused as `CLAIM_UNCONFIRMED` **without running** (the loser of a race whose verdict was lost no longer executes locally); tails are re-cut to `tail_bytes` after scrubbing so a scrubbed tail cannot exceed the wire cap and strand the result; saving a `run_on_host` definition now also requires the signer to own the `project` coordinate (an admin of any channel could otherwise republish a victim project's public entry under the victim's coordinate and approve it himself); the desktop reads the refusal code from `refusal_code` as `host_step_output` writes it; `parse_actions_yml` trims the bound name.
   - **Not done / disclosed gaps.** (0) Who may claim and report is bare channel membership (`host_steps.rs` `admit`): any member can claim a step and never report, or report a fabricated exit; spec § 5.4's "exactly one host" is enforced, *which* hosts is not — a served-host roster is C2/C4 work. The REST host-step row exposes `artifact_ref`, the claiming host's absolute state path, to every channel member; the 46014 echo carries tails and the path by design. A crash between the 46013 publish and `set_host_step_requested_event` leaves `requested_event_id` null, and both handlers then skip the "names the recorded request" check. No startup sweep re-arms a `waiting_host` run whose row is already closed; only the claiming host's retry does. (1) Nothing exercised live: no relay redeploy, no provider on the installed app, no `bee workflows trigger → 46010 → grant → 46013 → 46023 → 46014` end to end; the proof in § 7 C1 is still owed. (2) No expiry sweep: an unclaimed request past `expires_at` refuses claims but the run stays `waiting_host` until something fails it; same for approvals past `expires_at` (pre-existing). (3) A `request_approval` step whose `from:` is not `any` or a 64-hex key now parks the run instead of failing it, and `check_approver_spec` still refuses every grant against such a spec — the run waits until it expires; the honest fix is C4's `project-owner:<coord>`. (4) A 46023 refusal published before a claim (drift, no checkout) is stored but leaves the row `requested`, so another host may still claim; if every host refuses, the run waits. (5) The `allow future runs` checkbox is rendered disabled; `scope: action` is C4. (6) Project scoping is carried as `WorkflowDef.project` inside the definition, not yet a `workflows.project_ref` column with an `a`-tag index (C2).

151. **Project actions C2 built: `workflows.project_ref`, the `a` tag and the 30624 admission rule, `ref_updated` from git pushes, schedule timezones, `manual` (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.3, § 7 C2 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). What is built, with the code that proves it:
   - **Project scoping on the relay.** Migration 0044 adds `workflows.project_ref` (TEXT, partial index; `schema/schema.sql` mirrors it). `handle_workflow_def` (`crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/command_executor.rs`) takes `project_ref` from the definition's own `project`; an `a` tag is optional but must equal it, and an `a` tag on a definition that declares no project is refused. A project-scoped write is admitted by exactly the kind:30624 rule — project creator, roster Owner, or a founder of an endorsed repository — through `pack_source::project_write_admitted`, which is `pack_source_write_admitted` with its decode lifted out (`crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/pack_source.rs`); this replaces C1's narrower "coordinate owner" check. `handle_workflow_trigger` admits, besides the workflow owner, a project Owner or Collaborator from `get_project_role_by_coordinate` (the roster has no "Admin"; Viewers may not run). `bee actions publish` now sets the `a` tag (`buzz_sdk::build_project_workflow_def`).
   - **`ref_updated`.** `TriggerDef::RefUpdated { ref (glob), repository? }` (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs`; `*` stops at `/`, `**` crosses it, via `globset` with `literal_separator`; a trigger without `repository` requires `project`). `WorkflowEngine::on_repo_state` (`lib.rs`) diffs the parent and committed ref maps, loads `list_enabled_ref_updated_workflows` (`definition->'trigger'->>'on' = 'ref_updated'`, `crates/buzz-db/src/workflow.rs`), matches by exact repository coordinate or, for triggers without one, by the pushed repository's `git_repo_names.project_ref` against the workflow's `project_ref`, rechecks owner authority, and starts one run per matching changed ref with `trigger.repository/ref/before/after/pusher` in the context (`TriggerContext`, `executor.rs`; a created or deleted ref has an empty `before`/`after`). The git transport calls it in `fire_ref_updated_workflows` right after the kind:30618 is stored and fanned out (`crates/buzz-relay/src/api/git/transport.rs`), spawned so the push response never waits; never from the pre-receive path, so a denied push cannot fire, and a no-op push (no 30618) is silent. Proof at engine level against Postgres: `on_repo_state_fires_ref_updated_for_the_repositorys_project` (`lib.rs` tests, `#[ignore]`, run 2026-09-17 on the local dev DB at migration 0044: 1 passed) — a push moving `refs/heads/main` starts one run for the project's own workflow with the ref and both commits in its context, none for another project's, and a tag-only push starts none.
   - **Schedule timezone.** `Schedule.timezone` (IANA, `chrono-tz`, validated at parse); `cron_fire_instant` evaluates in the zone and converts to UTC before the durable claim, so the `(community, workflow, scheduled_for)` key is unchanged. `actions.yml`'s top-level `timezone` is applied to every schedule without its own **before hashing**, so the stored definition carries the zone explicitly and the host's recompilation agrees (`actions_file.rs`, test `file_timezone_is_applied_to_schedules_without_their_own`). Proof: `cron_fire_instant_honours_the_definition_timezone_across_dst` — Friday 17:00 America/New_York is 22:00Z on 2026-03-06 and 21:00Z on 2026-03-13, and 02:30 on 2026-03-08 (the skipped hour) is never produced.
   - **Amendments to the spec text.** The 30620 `d` is a UUID v5 of `<project>\n<name>` (the relay's `d` must be a UUID); roster roles are Owner/Collaborator/Viewer, so "Admin" maps to Collaborator; `ci_result` stays C5.
   - **Not done / disclosed gaps.** Nothing exercised live: no push against a deployed relay, no scheduled fire observed across a real DST change; both proofs are engine-level. `check_owner_authority` still gates a `ref_updated` run on the owner's *channel* role, not the project roster. A `ref_updated` trigger fires once per matching ref per push; a push that moves twenty branches under `refs/heads/*` starts twenty runs. The desktop Actions tab labels the trigger but does not yet show the pushed ref on the run row.

152. **Compose provenance on the wire: `composeRef` on 44223, the bundle manifest mirror, and the Roles page's template-drift line — slice A4's wire half (2026-09-17).** Spec § 4.6, § 7 A4 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). Built, with the code that proves it:
   - **The key.** `SessionMetadata.compose_ref: Option<ComposeRef { app_version, digest }>` (`crates/buzz-core/src/coding_session_payload.rs`), the ninth independent additive key on 44223 metadata, following the `packRef` amendment pattern exactly: omitted when absent, an explicit null refused by name, unknown fields refused, and — the one new rule — refused without a `packRef`, because a composition of nothing is not a fact. `digest` must be `sha256:` plus sixty-four lowercase hex. Test `decode_metadata_accepts_the_compose_ref_shape_only_beside_a_pack_ref` covers absence, round trip, the orphan, the null, a bad digest and an extra key.
   - **The producer.** The provider reads the staged pack's `compose.json` (`buzz_persona::compose::read_provenance`, new; an unreadable or off-schema file is an error, a missing one is `None`) when it builds the seat's skills (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/lib.rs` `seat_compose_ref`), stores it on the session record (`state.rs` `SessionRecord.compose_ref`, serde-defaulted so older records load), and publishes it on the create, restore and status paths beside `pack_ref`. A `compose.json` that exists but cannot be read is logged and disclosed as nothing rather than as a made-up composition (test `a_composed_pack_discloses_its_compose_ref_and_an_uncomposed_one_does_not`). The seat bundle's `manifest.json` carries the same object as `composeRef` (`crates/buzz-persona/src/skills.rs` `write_bundle_manifest`).
   - **The reader.** The desktop decodes `composeRef` with the Rust rules (`codingSessionPackRef.ts` `readComposeRef`; `codingSessionIngressPayloads.ts` refuses it alone, null or malformed), carries it on the catalog record, and the Roles page's reported rows say `Composed with Beekeeper X, this computer's version` / `… this computer is Y, whose templates may differ` / `… this computer's version is not known yet` (`rolesCopy.ts` `templateDriftText`; `rolePackSnapshots.ts` `composedWith`, `thisComputerVersion` from `getVersion()` in `useProjectPacksView.ts`). The line claims only that the catalogs differ, never that the text does.
   - **A gate hole found on the way, and closed.** C2 (item 151) landed with four provider tests broken: its `actions.yml` fixture paired a webhook trigger with a `run_on_host` step, which C2 itself began refusing, and C2's gate ran the workflow, db, relay, CLI and SDK suites but not the provider's. Fixed here by switching the fixture to `manual` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_steps.rs` tests); the lesson for the next slice is that the provider crate belongs in every actions gate because it consumes the workflow schema.
   - **Not done.** A seat staged before this landed carries no `composeRef` and its row says nothing about composition. The desktop does not yet compare `composeRef.digest` against what this computer would compose now (that needs the same source bytes staged locally; § 4.9's definition drift already answers the sharper question for the worktree case). Nothing exercised on an installed app; the § 7 A4 live proof — edit a role on `main`, watch the card, restart, read the new briefing — is still owed.

153. **Project actions C3 built: `wake_agent` routes a host step's result to a persistent agent (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.2, § 5.7, § 7 C3 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). Built, with the code that proves it:
   - **The step.** `ActionDef::WakeAgent { to: {agent}, brief }` (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs`); requires a top-level `project`; the brief may use `{{trigger.*}}` and `{{steps.<id>.output.*}}`. Mode (2)'s `brief: {on_success, on_failure}` is expanded by `parse_actions_yml` into `<id>_success` / `<id>_failure` with opposite `if:` on the nearest preceding `run_on_host`'s exit code, **before hashing**, so relay and host see the same two steps (`actions_file.rs` `expand_wake_brief_sugar`; test `a_two_way_brief_expands_into_two_gated_wake_steps`). Mode (1) is just a `wake_agent` with its own `if:`.
   - **The engine** treats it as a host step with no approval gate: the executor suspends with `Suspension::HostStep { step_kind: "wake_agent", inputs }` where `inputs` is the earlier steps' outputs keyed by id (`executor.rs`, `suspend.rs`), and the kind:46013 carries `stepKind: wake_agent` and `inputs` (`crates/buzz-core/src/host_step.rs`, additive, default `{}`); the result may carry `routed {agent, role, sessionId, sessionRef?, commandId}`. `dispatch_action` now receives the step outputs.
   - **The host** (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_route.rs`): recompiles the step from its own `actions.yml` (the brief never rides the wire), resolves the agent's name to a role through `beekeeper/team.yml` (`resolve_wake_role`), picks that role's newest open execution for the project **on this computer** (`pick_open_execution`), renders the brief into the spec's `action_result` envelope with the trigger context and the earlier steps' outputs (`wake_brief_text`), and — after the claim — publishes a provider-signed kind:44220 boundary turn whose command id is a pure function of run and step (`route_command_id`), writes a kind:44246 observed gate row into the woken session naming the preceding host step's outcome (`gate_row_for`), and reports a 46023 with `routed`. A missing `team.yml`, an unknown agent, no open execution here, or a relay refusal are refused by name (`ROUTE_NO_TEAM`, `ROUTE_UNKNOWN_AGENT`, `ROUTE_NO_SESSION`, `ROUTE_REJECTED`), the first three before any claim so another host may still take the step. Exactly once across a duplicate 46013 and a restart: the store refuses a recorded request, the operation ledger fences the run's step, and the deterministic command id converges on the receiving command ledger. Tests in `action_route.rs`; `verify_request` branches on `stepKind` (`action_steps.rs`).
   - **Surfaces.** The REST host-step row carries `routed_agent` and `routed_command_id`; the Actions tab row reads `routed to <agent> · turn action-route-<8 hex>` (`actionRunLabel.ts`).
   - **Not done / disclosed.** No execution is created when none is open (persistent agents' "one umbrella the host creates on first route" needs desktop-staged seat custody; C5), and an execution served by another host is not woken — both are `ROUTE_NO_SESSION`. `provider_may_wake` is not checked here; the turn is admitted or refused by the receiving provider's ordinary authority decision, which is the same provider for a local execution, and the refusal reaches the run only through the turn's receipt, not the 46023. The live proof — a failing build waking the builder once across a duplicate delivery and a restart — is still owed.

154. **Project actions C4 built: the autorun grant — `scope: action`, hash binding, kind 46032 revoke, kind 46015 record, the inbox checkbox (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.4, § 7 C4 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). Built, with the code that proves it:
   - **The grant.** A kind:46030's content is now `{"note", "scope": "run" | "action"}` (`crates/buzz-core/src/workflow_autorun.rs` `decode_approval_grant_content`); plain text or an empty content is read as a note with `scope: run`, so a pre-C4 desktop or `bee` never grants more than it asked, and a JSON object with an unknown key is refused rather than read as a note. `scope: action` makes the relay also insert a `workflow_autorun_grants` row (migration 0045; `crates/buzz-db/src/workflow.rs` `create_autorun_grant`) bound to the workflow's `definition_hash` **as stored at that moment**, and publish a relay-signed kind:46015 `AutorunChanged { change: granted }` (`command_executor.rs` `handle_approval_grant`, `publish_autorun_changed`).
   - **The skip.** The executor's `run_on_host` arm asks `find_active_autorun_grant(workflow, definition_hash)` before it asks for this run's own approval; a match releases the step with `approval: {approvalRef: <grant event id>, scope: action}` on the 46013 (`executor.rs`). Because the binding is the hash, an edit re-arms the gate with no revocation — proved end to end against Postgres by `an_autorun_grant_skips_the_gate_until_the_definition_changes` (`lib.rs` tests, `#[ignore]`, run 2026-09-17 on the dev DB at 0045: 1 passed): granted → straight to the host with no approval row; edited → gated; restored and revoked → gated.
   - **Who may approve.** The synthetic gate on a project action now names `project-owner:<coord>`, and `approver_admitted` (`command_executor.rs`) admits the project's creator or a roster Owner (`get_project_role_by_coordinate`); a plain workflow's gate still names its owner's key. The pre-C1 `any` / 64-hex forms are unchanged.
   - **Revocation.** Kind:46032 (`AutorunRevoke`, `d` = workflow id, `h` = channel) is admitted from the workflow owner or, for a project action, anyone the kind:30624 writer rule admits (`project_write_admitted`); it stamps `revoked_at` on every unrevoked grant — rows are never deleted — and publishes a 46015 `revoked`. Registered in the command dispatch, ingest scope and metrics label; 46015 is relay-only and inside the loop guard (`is_workflow_execution_kind` → 46015).
   - **Surfaces.** REST `GET /workflows/{id}/autorun` lists grants newest first, each with `matches_current`, plus `active`. The Actions tab's approval row has a live "allow future runs of this action" checkbox (`ProjectActionRunRow.tsx`, → `grantApproval(ref, note, "action")`); the action card shows `autorun · granted by <who>` with a Revoke button, or `autorun granted for an earlier definition · approval re-armed` when the only unrevoked grant no longer matches (`ProjectActionCard.tsx`, `useProjectActions.ts`). The desktop's grant builder emits the JSON form; `bee workflows approve --allow-future-runs` does the same.
   - **Not done / disclosed.** The 46015 is announced after the grant row is committed, so a reader that saw the row before the event saw it first; a publish failure is logged and the row stands. An approval row does not record its own scope, so an approval's "this run | this action" reads off the autorun listing, not the approval. Nothing exercised on a deployed relay; the live proof is still owed.

155. **Project actions C5 built: `hire_agent` (the ephemeral agent), agent-managed mode, and the `ci_result` trigger (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.2, § 5.3, § 5.7, § 7 C5 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). Built, with the code that proves it:
   - **`hire_agent { role, session: {agent}, brief }`** (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs`; the role must pass `validate_role_slug`, `project` required) is a host step with no approval gate (`executor.rs`; `HOST_STEP_KIND_HIRE_AGENT` in `crates/buzz-core/src/host_step.rs`). The host recompiles it from its own `actions.yml`, resolves the session agent to a role through `team.yml` and to that role's open execution here, requires that execution to name an umbrella and genesis (`HIRE_NO_UMBRELLA` otherwise), renders the brief with the same `action_result` envelope a wake uses, and — after the claim — publishes a provider-signed kind:44221 `session.hire` into that umbrella with a command id that is a pure function of run and step (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_route.rs` `build_hire_event`, `hire_command_id`; `action_steps.rs` `route_hire`). The desktop answers the hire as it answers a lead's: it stages the seat's custody and creates the seat. The result's `routed` carries `hiredRole`; the Actions tab row reads `hired a <role> into <agent>'s session · hire <id>`. A brief over the hire ceiling refuses `HIRE_BRIEF_TOO_LONG`; a relay refusal — the `may_hire` rule admits the umbrella's founder, a granted operator, or an active lead hiring a non-lead role, and this host's key must be one of those — reaches the run as `HIRE_REJECTED`.
   - **Agent-managed mode (spec § 5.2 mode 3)** is exactly a `hire_agent` whose brief tells the seat which command to run and watch; nothing more was needed.
   - **`ci_result { check, conclusion: [...] }`** (`schema.rs`; `project` required, at least one conclusion). The engine's loop guard now lets a kind:46008 through (`lib.rs` `on_event`: `is_workflow_execution_kind` still refuses every other 460xx kind), decodes it once with `decode_ci_result`, and fires a `ci_result` workflow only when the result's `identity.project` equals the workflow's `project_ref`, the check names match, and the conclusion is listed. `build_trigger_context` exposes `{{trigger.commit}}`, `check`, `conclusion`, `evidence_url` and `repository` for a 46008 and leaves `text` empty. The context's trigger-specific fields answer only when set, so a webhook body's `commit` keeps resolving as before (`executor.rs` `get_field`; the existing `record_ci_result_templates_only_callback_owned_fields` test caught the shadowing).
   - **A gate note.** The first desktop test run of this slice reported 1 failure of 9,654 with no `not ok` line naming a test; two immediate reruns passed 9,654 of 9,654, and the label tests of this slice pass in isolation. Treated as a flake, recorded here so a repeat has a first sighting.
   - **Not done / disclosed.** The hire's admission at the relay is the existing `may_hire` rule; a provider whose key is neither the umbrella's founder nor a granted operator has its hire refused, and nothing here grants it. No engine-level Postgres proof for the 46008 path (the relay stores 46008 through its own CI-result insert; the unit tests cover the decode and matching pure functions). The live proof — a runner seated in the project manager's umbrella, a CI failure waking the project manager — is still owed.



## 2a. Direction settled 2026-08-18

Three independent answers to "what should a new execution get on its first
turn" — two blind design reviews and Sol's implementation — converged on: push
a small brief the agent would not know to ask for, pull the rest, never inject
raw transcripts. Sol's shipped answer goes further and emits only what the
record already proves (turn outcomes, tool attempt outcomes, cited event ids)
rather than a model-written summary, because a generated summary manufactures
a new unverified claim. That is the shipped direction. Distillation of older
material is still worth building, but it must cite those evidence ids rather
than replace them, and it is not started.

156. **Project actions C6 built: a worktree at the triggering commit, artifact upload, and the scrubbing audit (2026-09-17).** Spec § 5.6, § 7 C6 ([`PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md`](PROJECT_TEAMS_AND_ACTIONS_SPEC.md)). Built, with the code that proves it:
   - **Worktree.** `run_on_host.checkout: current | triggering_commit` (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs` `HostCheckout`, default `current`); `triggering_commit` is refused at save time unless the trigger is `ref_updated` or `ci_result`. On the host (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_steps.rs` `spawn_host_step`; `host_command.rs` `triggering_commit`, `cut_worktree`, `remove_worktree`): the commit is `after` for a push or `commit` for a CI result (a deleted ref names none → `ACTION_NO_TRIGGER_COMMIT`, refused before the claim); after the claim the host checks the commit is local, fetches all remotes once if not, refuses `ACTION_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE` if it still is not, cuts `git worktree add --detach` under `<state_dir>/actions/<run>/<step>/worktree`, re-prepares the command against the worktree (so the working-directory escape check resolves there), runs, records `headSha`/`dirty` from the worktree, and removes it. `actions.yml` is still read from the recorded checkout, not the worktree: the hash check is against what the host holds, as § 5.6 says.
   - **Artifact upload.** `capture.upload: true` (default `false`) uploads `stdout.log` and `stderr.log` after scrubbing to the relay's Blossom `PUT /upload` with a kind:24242 auth naming the hash and the relay's authority (`artifact_upload.rs`, mirroring `bee upload`; the relay's `/upload` accepts non-image files, only the legacy `/media/upload` refuses them). The result carries `artifacts: [{name, url, sha256, bytes}]` (`crates/buzz-core/src/host_step.rs`, at most 8, sha256 of the exact bytes uploaded); the REST host-step row exposes them and the Actions tab row links them as `logs: stdout.log, stderr.log`. An upload failure is logged and the result goes out without that artifact; the run is not failed for it.
   - **Scrubbing audit.** `host_command::scrub` replaces exact substrings of this host's `env_from_host` values, now only when the value is at least 4 bytes (`MIN_SCRUB_SECRET_BYTES`; a one-character value would erase the log while hiding nothing). It is applied to the tails on the 46023 and, via `scrub_bytes`, to the uploaded logs; the on-disk logs stay unscrubbed (host-local). **What it does not catch, by construction:** a value the command printed base64- or URL-encoded, split across lines, or partially; and any secret from anywhere other than `env_from_host` (a token the command reads from a file or prints from its own config). That is why upload is off by default, and why the provider's own credentials are never in the child's environment at all (C1's fence).
   - **Not done / disclosed.** No retry on upload failure. A worktree left behind when `git worktree remove` fails stays under the state directory and is logged, not swept. The fetch before the cut is `git fetch --all`, so a checkout with no remote for the hive never sees the pushed commit and refuses. Nothing exercised on a deployed relay; every slice's live proof is still owed.

157. **A handover test read the adapter's log one line too early (2026-09-17).** `a_same_body_transfer_stops_the_old_claimants_queued_turn_too` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/tests/handover_integration_tests.rs`) failed CI on `main` twice in one day — Woodpecker pipelines 171 (`d8c16b7`) and 174 (`733f52cd6`, the C5 landing) — and passed on 172 and 173, with the same message each time: `and the new claimant's turn does reach the runtime … left: 1, right: 2`. Not a regression from either commit: the assertion counted `session/prompt` lines in the fake adapter's log straight after `pump_until_turn_started`, but the provider reports `TurnStarted` when it *sends* the prompt and the adapter writes the line when it *receives* it, so under CI load the count trails by one. Fixed by a bounded `wait_for_method_count` before the exact-count assertion (the other prompt-count site, after `TurnFinished`, was never racy). Consequence while it stood: `beekeeper-autodeploy` kept `89b3761c6` (C4) deployed through the C5 landing ("newest main pipeline (733f52cd6) is 'failure'"), so hive skipped a slice until the next green push. The locally seen desktop flake in item 155 is a different test.

158. **Roles and plans leave the code repository; each project gets `<slug>-beekeeper-agents` (Andy, 2026-09-18).** Decision, in Andy's words: "keeping both plans and agent instructions within the repository, even if filtered out, can lead to the agent wasting time discovering the instructions or reading the plans, or worse being influenced by out of date roles/plans which are irrelevant to the task at hand." Creating a project now auto-creates two relay repositories — `<slug>` for code, empty, and `<slug>-beekeeper-agents` for roles and plans — laid out as `roles/` and `plans/`, each with an `archive/` so the few roles that may read them can tell what is in force from what is retained. Answers given the same day: everything Beekeeper-specific leaves the code repository (`team.yml`, skills, `actions.yml` included); the seed *references* the shipped roles by include rather than copying them; the project's own agents repository is pinned by `ref: refs/heads/main`; spec first, then slices. Contract: spec § 1 item 5 and § 4.11; § 4.9 and § 4.10 struck; slices § 7 Part P; direction D19. What the pivot reverses, with the code that proves the state on this date: project creation publishes only the 30621 (`desktop/src/features/projects-container/useCreateProjectContainer.ts:127`); the in-repo layout hangs on four constants — `ACTIONS_YML = "beekeeper/actions.yml"` (`crates/buzz-workflow/src/actions_file.rs:23`), `TEAM_ROOT` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/action_route.rs:65`), `DEFAULT_FLAT_PATH` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/packs_cache.rs:52`), `READ_FENCED_ROLES_DIR` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/agent_fence.rs:325`) — plus the sparse exclusion (`desktop/src-tauri/src/coding_sessions/worktree.rs:601-651`), `roles_visible` (`crates/buzz-persona/src/team.rs:61-68`) and the branch override, which already answers `OtherRepository` across repositories (`packs_cache/branch_override.rs:95-113`); the composer is root-relative and never learns the directory's name (`crates/buzz-persona/src/compose.rs:141,810-830`), so the move costs it nothing. What already exists to build on: the announce → seed → push → 30624 → withdraw sequence for `<slug>-packs` (`packs_repo.rs:322,476,660`; `crates/buzz-cli/src/commands/packs.rs:456,672`), repository ids as one namespace per community (`crates/buzz-db/src/git_repo.rs:31-40`), a seat pushing with its owner's tier (`crates/buzz-relay/src/api/git/policy_gate_tests.rs:285`), templates that carry skills (`crates/buzz-persona/src/template.rs:96-109`). The shipped packs under `personas/roles/` stay for rung 4 and legacy packs repositories but are **thin**: a persona of two include lines (`![[beekeeper/<role>@^1.0.0]]`, `![[beekeeper/working-contract@^1.0.0]]`), no skills of their own, manifest version `0.3.0`. Refuses a non-empty root (`.git` excepted), a catalog with no role template, or one missing a shared fragment. Test: the seed of the shipped catalog composes every role with its template's skills and the 2026-09-17 text.

The desktop's `DEFAULT_FLAT_PATH` stays `beekeeper` until P3, because the sparse exclusion still spells it.

160. **P1 built: creating a project creates its two repositories, and Finish setup finishes what did not land (2026-09-18).** Spec § 4.11, § 7 P1. With the code that proves it:

162. **P4 built: a role's `agents_repo` grant gives its seats the project's agents repository beside their worktree, and archived roles are listed (2026-09-18).** Spec § 4.11, § 7 P4. With the code that proves it:

A granted role whose source is not an agents repository (path not `.`), pins a sha rather than a branch, or has no worktree is **refused a seat** rather than seated without what its role needs.

On Claude a `read` clone joins the write fence as `Edit(//<clone>/**)` (`agent_fence::read_only_root_rules`); on Codex the sentence is the whole fence, as for every other boundary. Tests: the briefing for none/read/write; the read-only rule's spelling.

The clone is cut from the packs cache at the pinned branch's last sync, not refetched for the seat. `preview_coding_session_seat_pack` and `seat_definition_drift` still accept a `worktree` argument they no longer read.

A seed or push failure withdraws the agents announcement, leaves the project and code repository standing, and prints what landed with the remedy (`bee packs init --project …`). With `--repo` the command is unchanged. Tests: the two ids from a repository-shaped slug and refusal of a colon-bearing one; the taken-id refusal names id and owner and ignores the caller's own announcement.

So the setup flow cannot re-pin a project's agents repository to a pack-layout snapshot at a sha. What that leaves open, honestly: the project-team setup flow (`PROJECT_TEAM_SETUP_IMPL.md`) still authors the pack layout into a draft workspace and publishes `<slug>-packs-<hex>` at an immutable sha — a path no project created today can take. 164. **A created project had no default agents; creation now mints one per seeded role (2026-09-18, found by Andy on the local dev stack).** First live check of the pivot, on a local relay from `76a9751e5`: **New project** produced the head naming both repositories, both announcements and the source (`ref: refs/heads/main`, `path: .`), and the Agents tab was empty. The pivot had moved the *roles* into the agents repository but nothing minted the *identities* the old setup flow used to install from its pack-layout snapshot (`project_team_setup_activation::install_adopted_roles`), and that flow refuses a project with a source. Fix, with the code that proves it:
   - **Seed.** `team.yml` now lists one default agent per role — `{ name: <Title Case of the slug>, role, lifetime }`, the lead persistent and every other role ephemeral (`buzz_persona::seed`, `agent_display_name`) — so the names are the project's, in its repository, and `actions.yml` can route to them.
   - **Install.** `managed_agents/default_agents.rs` `install_default_agents(app, state, project, source)`: sync the agents clone, read `team.yml` (roles and names; role files alone when there is no manifest), stage every role through the composer, copy each staged pack to `<packs root>/installs/<owner8>-<id>/<role>/` — one stable directory per role, so a rerun refreshes the agents it already installed rather than minting a second set — scan that directory, and run the same installer the setup flow uses (`crew_roles::install_role_packs_in_named_team`) with identities minted the one way every managed agent is (`commands::mint_agent_identity`, a fresh key with the owner's NIP-OA attestation), into the team "Project team <coord>"; then `associate_installation`, save personas/agents/teams, `retain_installed_agents`, the association backfill and the visibility verification, as the setup flow does. Run by `project_agents_init` after a seed that landed (so **Finish repository setup** installs them for a project created before this fix). A failure is `agentsError` on the result, never a failed create; the result carries `agentsInstalled` and the toast and the Finish setup panel print them.
   - **Second finding, same day (Andy).** With the install in place the lead picker on a new founded session still said "No NewTestTest agent with a role is on this computer" while the eight records sat on disk with `home_role` and `project_ref` set (verified in `managed-agents.json`). Cause: `useManagedAgentsQuery` re-reads only on the `agents-data-changed` event while no agent is running (`desktop/src/features/agents/hooks.ts`), and the installer saved records without raising it. Fix: `install_default_agents` emits `agents-data-changed` after saving, and the create mutation and Finish repository setup invalidate the managed-agents query when agents were installed.
   - **Not done / disclosed.** `bee projects create` cannot mint desktop-managed identities; a project created from the CLI gets its agents the first time the desktop's Finish repository setup runs for it. Nothing exercised beyond the local stack yet.

165. **Every crew-installed identity landed on the `buzz-agent` harness, so a hire of one was refused `HIRE_PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED` (2026-09-18, found by Andy on the local dev stack).** First team session on the pivot's NewTestTest project: the lead's hire of Verifier came back "Verifier is configured for buzz-agent, from the harness its record resolves to, buzz-agent, and this computer is running claude-primary, codex-primary". The refusal was right and the record was wrong.
   - **Cause, with the code.** Role packs are runtime-agnostic, so `install_role_packs_for_team` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/crew_roles.rs`) builds a record with `runtime: None` and stores the harness `record_agent_command` resolves for it, whose last tier is `default_agent_command()` = `buzz-agent` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/discovery.rs`) — the chat harness, which no coding-session provider runs. The hire reads an identity's runtime from that effective harness through the ACP catalog (item 136(b), `codingSessionHireAgentRuntime.ts`), the same way the Agents screen draws it, and refuses. Not specific to the new default-agent installer: the installed profile's fourteen Tank Loop identities on this Mac carry `runtime: null, agent_command: "buzz-agent"` too (`managed-agents.json`, read 2026-09-18), so a hire there refuses the same way; item 89's "every installed team identity has runtime null" described this state before 136(b) made it a refusal.
   - **Fix.** `crew_roles::pin_default_runtime(result, preferred)` (`crew_roles_runtime.rs`) pins this computer's `preferred_runtime` (global agent config) onto each identity the install wrote that pins none and re-derives its stored harness (`derive_harness_fields`, factored out of the install loop). All three installers apply it — `default_agents.rs`, `project_team_setup_activation.rs`, `commands/crew_roles.rs` — the same seed `apply_persona_snapshot` gives an agent created from a definition (`commands/personas/snapshot.rs`). A pack-declared or host-seated runtime is left alone; no preference pins nothing, and the record stays honest about that. Tests: `a_fresh_install_pins_the_hosts_preferred_runtime_and_the_harness_follows`, `the_default_runtime_never_moves_an_identity_the_host_already_seated`, `no_preferred_runtime_pins_nothing` (`crew_roles_runtime_tests.rs`).
   - **Second finding while here.** Item 139 claimed "both TS consumers" read the host's `effective_runtime`; the resolver did, but `codingSessionHireAgentsFromManaged` (`codingSessionHireCandidates.ts`) never passed it, so the hire path always ran the catalog reconstruction. Now wired, with `"global"` admitted to `runtimeSource` — the host reports the tier it stopped at, with a null value, when no tier pins a runtime. Test "the host's candidate list carries the host's effective runtime to the decision" (`codingSessionHireProjectScope.test.mjs`). Struck in 139 where it stands.
   - **Not migrated.** Existing identities keep `runtime: null` until reinstalled: for NewTestTest, Project settings → Finish repository setup reruns the install and pins them; the installed profile's Tank Loop identities need a reinstall through one of the three installers or their runtime set on the Agents screen, the refusal's own remedy.

166. **The answer-stall guard closed a lead's turn that had not answered, over narration it had streamed before its tool calls (2026-09-18, found by Andy on the local dev stack).** Second team session on NewTestTest (session `265da374-f4d6-41fe-8e02-c31e96d7bcb4`, turn `e1479f7c…`): the lead narrated, ran nine tools, and its last two — the `buzz-session-context` MCP reads `session_overview` and `session_inbox` — returned at +23.9s (signed 44225 seq 21–23). Then nothing. At +144s the provider published `turn_wire: … quiet 120.0s; 0 tools in flight; answer streamed` and `answer_stall_recovered: @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp 0.70.0 answered but never resolved this prompt; Beekeeper closed the turn after 120s. The answer above is complete.` (seq 24–25). No answer existed: the turn decided nothing and hired no one, and the session sat idle with the lead's job undone.
   - **Cause, with the code.** `AnswerStallWatch` (`crates/buzz-acp/src/acp.rs`) armed on `answer_streamed && tools_in_flight.is_empty()`, and `answer_streamed` was set by any top-level `agent_message_chunk` in the turn and never cleared. Claude narrates before it calls tools ("I'll orient first…", seq 3, 10, 17), so every tool-using turn was armed the moment its last tool result landed, and any silence there — the agent's next API call, or the agent stuck — was read as "the answer streamed and the prompt response never came", the shape item 59 built the guard for. The nudge then published the guard's fixed sentence, which was false for this shape.
   - **Fix.** A top-level `tool_call` now clears `answer_streamed`: only prose since the last tool call is the answer, so silence after a tool result falls to the idle budget (`DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS`, 870s) and earns its honest disclosure, and the stall sentence is true by construction. Test `narration_before_a_tool_call_does_not_arm_the_stall_watch` beside item 59's three; `turn_wire`'s "answer streamed" now means prose since the last tool call.
   - **What is not settled.** Why Claude Code produced nothing after the MCP results. Its own transcript (`~/.claude/projects/-Users-andy-Code-mintet-wt-mini-tet-2-lead/d97bbead-….jsonl`) records both MCP `tool_result`s at 00:12:31Z and then only `[Request interrupted by user]` at 00:14:32Z — no assistant message, no logged API error — so it either never started the next request or that request returned nothing in 120s; item 54's upstream shape (claude-code #88378, claude-agent-acp #970) fits and is unproven here. The dev app runs its provider without `RUST_LOG` or `BUZZ_CSP_EMIT_RAW_SDK_FRAMES` (both are read from the app's environment per provider spawn, `desktop/src-tauri/src/session_provider/supervisor.rs`), so the provider log holds only start lines and there is no adapter stderr to read. The next stall on the dev stack should be run with both set. Recovery for this session is the one item 54 names: a new message to the lead wakes it.

167. **A hire was answered from a stale React Query snapshot of the workdir store, so `HIRE_CHECKOUT_NOT_RECORDED` outlived the write that should have cleared it (2026-09-19, live on the installed `edbc430dd` build).** Brian created project Pivot Test, set its repository folder in Project settings → This computer (the store held `byProject[…pivot-test]` from 10:56:53Z), founded a Team session, and the lead's two hires at 10:58Z were both refused "this computer has no repository folder recorded for Pivot Test" — over a minute after the store had the answer on disk. Same class as the August finding in item 136(a)/the "HIRE_NO_ROUTE" memory note: a hire decided from a cached snapshot of host state rather than the state itself.
   - **Cause, with the code.** `CodingSessionHireHost.tsx` read the workdir store through `useQuery({ queryKey: ["coding-session-workdir-state"], queryFn: getCodingSessionWorkdirState })` (around line 86, pre-fix) and built `checkoutForHire` from that query's `workdirs.data` (around line 144). `ProjectSettingsLocalSection.tsx`'s `commit()` (around line 116, the `setCodingSessionWorkdir` call) and `handleClear()` wrote the native store directly and never invalidated that query key, so the host kept answering from whatever it had fetched at mount — in this run, from before the write.
   - **Fix, both halves.** (1) `checkoutForHire` in `CodingSessionHireHost.tsx` no longer reads any query cache at all: it calls `getCodingSessionWorkdirState()` — the same native command the query used — fresh, at the exact moment each hire is honoured, and the now-unused `workdirs` query was deleted from the component (it rendered nothing, so nothing else there read it). `checkoutForHire`'s type in `useCodingSessionHire.ts` widened to allow a promise, and `honour()` now awaits it; a synchronous function (every existing test's shape) still works, since `await` on a plain value resolves it immediately. (2) `ProjectSettingsLocalSection.tsx`'s `commit()` and `handleClear()` now call `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["coding-session-workdir-state"] })` after a successful write, so the Roles tab redirect (`app/routes/index.tsx`) and `useRolePacksProject.ts`, which still render from that cache, catch up too.
   - **Not fixed here, disclosed.** Other writers to the same store were found by `grep` and are outside this lane's ownership: `founded/TeamReadinessUseThisFolder.tsx`'s "use this folder" button, `ProjectsManagePanel.tsx`'s own `setCodingSessionWorkdir` call, and the create-hint writers in `useNewCodingSessionCreate.ts`, `useCodingSessionCrewLaunch.ts` and `codingSessionHandoverPublish.ts` do not invalidate the query key either. The hire path no longer depends on any of them being fixed — it never reads the cache — but the Roles tab and `useRolePacksProject` can still render a stale answer after any of those writes until they are covered too.
   - **Evidence.** `CodingSessionHireHost.test.mjs`: "a hire answered after a store write sees the new checkout, with no refetch" mounts the real `checkoutForHire` shape against a mocked native command whose answer changes after the harness's own settle loop, with no query or refetch involved. `ProjectSettingsLocalSection.test.mjs` (new file): both `commit()` and `handleClear()` invalidate `["coding-session-workdir-state"]` on a live `QueryClient`. Not exercised against a live hire on an installed build.

168. **Every credentialed git operation the installed app ran after a relaunch failed with `could not read Username`, because a Finder-launched bundle reaches Apple's git 2.39.5, which cannot carry a Nostr credential at all (2026-09-19, found and reproduced 07:10 EDT on the installed `edbc430dd` bundle).** Item 167 is taken by a concurrent lane; this is 168.
   - **What was seen.** `~/Library/Logs/io.agiterra.beekeeper.app/beekeeper.2026-09-19.log:10` — `2026-09-19T11:06:51.781529Z WARN buzz_lib::managed_agents::actor_seats: refusing to seat an agent without the pack its project promised … reason="fatal: could not read Username for 'https://hive.agiterra.org/git/…': terminal prompts disabled"` — repeated across the re-stage of 43 recorded seats (23 such lines in that log), and then on two hires of a new project whose pack source pins a *branch* and so must fetch. Reproduced outside the app with the exact `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` environment `configure_git_auth` writes: the same fetch fails under `/usr/bin/git` and succeeds under `/opt/homebrew/bin/git`. On this Mac, `/usr/bin/git --version` → `git version 2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)`; `/opt/homebrew/bin/git --version` → `git version 2.55.0`.
   - **Cause, with the code (line numbers at `edbc430dd`).** `git-credential-nostr` answers over git's `authtype` credential protocol and prints *nothing* when git does not announce `capability[]=authtype` (`crates/git-credential-nostr/src/lib.rs:318-345`, `:411`, `:481-482`); that capability exists from git **2.46**. The app resolved git with `resolve_command("git")` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/project_git_exec.rs:390,402,426`), which in a bundle falls through to `PATH`, and a Finder-launched app's `PATH` is `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. So git never asked the helper for a credential and fell straight to the username prompt — an error about a credential, for a problem that is the git. `tauri dev` from a terminal inherits a `PATH` with Homebrew's git and never sees it; the 2026-09-16 hires never fetched, because their packs were commit-pinned and already cached (item 135).
   - **Fix.** A new `desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/project_git_version.rs` probes candidate gits with `--version` in order — the resolved `PATH` git, then `/opt/homebrew/bin/git`, `/usr/local/bin/git`, `/opt/homebrew/opt/git/bin/git`, then the workspace's `bin/git` — and picks the first at 2.46 or newer, cached in a `OnceLock` for the app's life. No login shell is consulted. `GitAuthConfig` carries `remote_git: Result<PathBuf, String>`, and `run_git_status`/`run_git_bytes` take it only for an invocation that needs credentials (`git_for`); local-only work keeps whatever git was found, so a machine with only Apple's git still does everything that does not reach the relay.
   - **Refusal instead of git's username error.** With no capable git, every remote operation fails with one sentence: "git 2.39.5 at /usr/bin/git cannot authenticate to the relay: the Nostr credential helper needs git 2.46 or newer. Install it with `brew install git` and relaunch." The helper prints the same explanation to stderr when it is invoked without the `authtype` capability (`authtype_unsupported_message`), so a terminal user reads it too instead of silence.
   - **Disclosure.** The Settings → About build row gains `git <version> at <path>`, in destructive colour with "too old to authenticate to the relay" below 2.46 (`aboutGitLine`, `desktop/src/features/settings/ui/aboutBuildRowCopy.ts`; read over the new `get_git_capability` command). Team readiness gains one fact, `GIT_TOO_OLD_FOR_RELAY` (category `host`): **Limited** normally, **Blocked** when the project's pack source could not be read — which is exactly the shape a branch pin or an uncached commit produces, since both must fetch and a fetch is what this git cannot do. `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` state the requirement under their prerequisites.
   - **Workaround that was in force, and is no longer needed.** `launchctl setenv PATH /opt/homebrew/bin:…` before relaunch. It made the bundle inherit a Homebrew `PATH`; it fixed nothing about a machine whose `PATH` nobody edited.
   - **Not done.** Nothing was exercised against hive: the fix is proven by unit tests (version parsing including Apple's line, candidate order, the ≥ 2.46 pick with a fake probe, the refusal sentence, the About copy, the readiness fact) and by the environment reproduction above, not by a live hire on an installed bundle. `buzz-cli`'s own git spawns were not audited; they run from a terminal, where `PATH` already carries a modern git.

169. **A seat granted the agents repository could not be staged at all — git refused the clone's `file` transport — and the hire it killed was never answered (2026-09-19, live on the installed `edbc430dd` bundle; the code is Andy's P4, item 162, and he should review this).** Two bugs on one path: the clone could not run, and the failure had no answer. Project Pivot Test, source pinned `refs/heads/main` with `path: .`, `team.yml` giving `runner` `workspace.agents_repo: read`; the lead hired a runner at 07:24 EDT.
   - **Bug 1, the transport, with the code.** The host cut the seat's worktree `/Users/brian/Projects/pivot-test-wt-coding-session-runner-1` at 11:24:31Z, then `stage_coding_session_actor_seat` called `cut_seat_agents_clone` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/actor_seats.rs:822`), which runs `git clone --quiet --branch main -- <packs cache path> <worktree>-agents` with `build_git_auth_config(state)` (`seat_agents_clone.rs:37-49` before the fix). That configuration sets `protocol.file.allow=never` — `configure_git_auth` writes it from `allow_file_transport: false`, which **every** production constructor in `desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/project_git_exec.rs` set — so git refused outright: `fatal: transport 'file' not allowed`. Reproduced by hand with the same `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` entries: the clone fails with that exact sentence, and with `protocol.file.allow=always` the same command succeeds. So **no seat with an `agents_repo` grant could ever be staged**; item 162's clone had never run.
   - **Fix 1.** A local configuration for the one case whose remote is a path this host wrote itself: `build_local_clone_git_auth_config` (`project_git_exec.rs:445`) takes `build_local_git_auth_config` — no credential helper, no nsec in the environment — and allows the `file` transport. `cut_seat_agents_clone` uses it for the clone and for the `git remote set-url origin <relay url>` that follows (`seat_agents_clone.rs:90`), which is unchanged otherwise. The remote configuration is **not** widened: a relay-supplied clone URL must still never be able to name a local path.
   - **Decision: the clone still comes from the packs cache, not from the relay.** Spec § 4.11 says "clones the repository from its packs cache", and item 162's "not refetched for the seat" stands. `origin` is pointed at the relay immediately after the clone, so a `write` seat has a real upstream from its first command — `git fetch` brings it to the relay's tip, `git push` goes to the relay under the seat's own credentials and its owner's tier. Cutting from the relay URL instead would put a network clone inside every hire, would need the *host's* credentials for a repository the seat is meant to authenticate to, and would refetch bytes the cache holds by definition (the host had just synced it to stage this seat's role pack). Recorded in the module doc.
   - **Bug 2, the unanswered hire, with the code.** The failure above produced no refusal on the relay: the lead's `bee sessions hire` reported "exit 5 unconfirmed" after 120 s with no seat, the provider's `refusals.jsonl` had no entry, and the worktree was left cut and recorded. `publishSeatedCodingSessionCreate` throws whatever staging threw (`codingSessionSeatedCreate.ts`, the `stageSeat` await), `honour()` had no `catch` of its own, and the effect's outer `.catch` recorded the thrown text as a host-local `error` outcome and published nothing. Everything before the create — membership, the project's 30624, key material, the § 4.11 clone — could therefore fail silently as far as the wire was concerned.
   - **Fix 2, one refusal, the tree disposed of, in the contract.** `HIRE_SEAT_STAGING_FAILED` joins all three pins in one commit (`crates/buzz-core/src/coding_session_lifecycle_command.rs:1159`, `hire_refusal_remedy` at `crates/buzz-cli/src/commands/sessions/crew.rs:2062`, `CODING_SESSION_HIRE_REFUSAL_CODES` at `desktop/src/features/coding-sessions/lib/codingSessionHirePolicy.ts:145`), so the TS↔core equality test and the CLI's remedy-coverage test both still hold. `refuseCodingSessionHireForSeatingFailure` (`codingSessionHireDisclosure.ts:171`) removes the tree the hire cut — the host's own prune, `prune_coding_session_seat_worktree` → `remove_recorded_seat_worktree`, which takes the recorded agents clone with it — and then publishes the refusal with the host's error text **verbatim** plus what happened to the tree; a prune that itself fails says so rather than being swallowed. `honour` calls it only when `createAttempted` is still false (`useCodingSessionHire.ts:822,838,876`): once `publish` has begun a 44221 may have reached the relay, and refusing there would claim no seat exists when one might, so that case keeps its old `error` outcome. `publishWithStagedSeat` also drops the custody entry when `stageSeat` throws (`codingSessionSeatedCreate.ts:234`), since the clone is cut before the entry is filed.
   - **Evidence.** Native, in throwaway temp repositories only: `a_clone_from_the_cache_needs_the_file_transport_only_the_local_config_allows` (`seat_agents_clone.rs`) asserts the remote configuration fails with `transport 'file' not allowed` and the local clone configuration succeeds — bug 1 as a red/green test. Desktop: "a staging failure is refused once, in the host's own words, and the tree it cut is removed", "a prune that fails is said in the refusal, not swallowed" and "a hire after the staging failure is fixed is seated normally" (`CodingSessionHireHost.test.mjs`, staging throwing the native sentence verbatim), the updated "the create is not published when custody staging fails" (`codingSessionSeatedCreate.test.mjs`), and the `HIRE_SEAT_STAGING_FAILED` remedy assertion in `crew_tests.rs`.
   - **Not done / disclosed.** Nothing exercised live: the first seat actually staged with an `agents_repo` grant is still owed, including a `write` seat's push. A failure *during* the create publish is still reported as a host-local error rather than a refusal, deliberately (above). The clone's content remains the cache's last sync. `bee`'s remedy for the new code tells the lead not to retry unchanged, which is a judgement about a host-local failure the lead cannot see.

170. **150 permanently rejected outbox rows starved every fresh publish: the provider's drain stopped at the first error on every pass (2026-09-19, observed 11:33–11:45Z on Brian's provider).** The ledger at `~/Library/Application Support/io.agiterra.beekeeper.app.dev/session-provider/1958c6c4…/outbox.jsonl` held 150 pending rows — 149 kind 44223 at `Priority::High` and 1 kind 44225 at `Priority::Normal` — of which **140 carried events created on 2026-09-04/05**, ages 15,000–21,000 minutes, in channels `79411448…` and `aa946c4e…`, from sessions long gone. The relay refuses any event whose `created_at` is more than 900 s from its clock (`crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs:3502` `MAX_TIMESTAMP_DRIFT_SECS`, message at `:3507` `"invalid: event timestamp too far from server time"`), so **not one of those 140 rows could ever publish**. `…/session-provider/logs/1958c6c4….log` showed `publish failed, will retry … kind=44225 attempts=36` about once a minute and **no successful publish for over ten minutes**; today's work — the kind 46022 claim of a host step, and seat metadata — never got a turn, and host-step run `537b718c…` sat in `waiting_host` because of it.
   - **Cause, with the code.** `Outbox::flush_limit` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/publish.rs`, `flush_limit` at line 487, drain order at 493) orders the eligible rows by `(priority, index)`, tries them in turn, and on the **first** `Err` sets a backoff and `break`s — the comment said a failure "almost always means the socket is gone". That is true of a dropped socket and false of a verdict. With 149 dead rows at high priority cycling through backoff, the first eligible row on nearly every pass was a dead one, so the pass ended before it reached anything fresh. Nothing anywhere distinguished "the relay cannot deliver this right now" from "the relay will never accept these bytes", and nothing ever removed an unpublishable row, so the ledger could only grow.
   - **Fix (a): a final verdict is not a retry.** `final_rejection_reason` (`publish.rs:91`) strips the envelope `RelayEventPublisher` wraps a negative NIP-01 `OK` in (`relay rejected durable event: `, written by `resolve_acknowledged_publish` in `crates/buzz-acp/src/relay.rs:1624-1634`) and matches the reason against `FINAL_REJECTION_PREFIXES` — `invalid:` (a verdict on the bytes) and `blocked:` (a verdict on the signer). The sink surfaces errors as `String` (`EventSink::publish`), and the trait is implemented outside this lane's ownership, so the classification is by NIP-01 reason prefix rather than by a new error type. Deliberately **not** final: `rate-limited:` and `error:` (the relay is asking for later, not never), `auth-required:` and `restricted:` (an authenticated or re-admitted socket changes the answer), and `duplicate:` (the relay already holds it). On a final reason the row is **parked** and the loop **continues**; only a transport error still backs off and breaks.
   - **Fix (b): never send what the relay cannot accept.** `RELAY_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS = 900` (`publish.rs:54`, commented with the `ingest.rs` line it mirrors) and `outside_relay_window` (`publish.rs:81`) gate both ends: `enqueue_inner` refuses an already-stale event without writing a ledger row, and `flush_limit` parks a row that aged out rather than spending a relay round trip on it. **Re-signing with a fresh timestamp was rejected as the default and is not implemented** (reasoning at `Outbox::park`, `publish.rs:636`): this outbox holds signed events, not the key that signed them, so it could not re-stamp one even if it should; and every kind that reaches it — lifecycle receipts, transcript items, turn claims — names a moment that has already passed, so a fresh `created_at` would publish a true-looking event with a false time. A disclosed gap is the honest outcome. No kind was found for which re-signing is right.
   - **Fix (c): a restart clears a poisoned ledger.** `Outbox::open` now runs `park_rows_outside_window` (`publish.rs:306`) after the existing rotated-key fence, parking every already-stale row and logging how many. The new ledger op is `LedgerRow::Park { id, kind, reason, at }` (`publish.rs:146`): finished exactly as an `Ack` is on replay (`publish.rs:231`), but carrying *why* and *when*, so the gap is explicable from the ledger rather than only from a log line. `Outbox::parked_len` (`publish.rs:346`) and `Provider::parked_publishes` (`crates/buzz-session-provider/src/lib.rs:8949`) disclose the count beside `pending_len`/`pending_publishes` — a queue that shrank because the relay refused its rows is not a queue that drained, and a status showing only the second would report health it does not have.
   - **Also changed.** `flush_limit`'s bounded budget now counts **sends**, not candidates, so `flush_one` cannot spend its one slot parking a row that costs no round trip — otherwise the starvation returns in slow motion.
   - **Evidence.** `publish.rs` tests: `a_final_rejection_is_parked_and_the_next_row_still_lands` (doomed row queued first and at high priority; the fresh row behind it lands in the *same* pass, and a reopen does not resurrect the parked one), `a_transport_error_still_backs_off_and_stops_the_pass`, `a_retryable_relay_reply_is_not_parked`, `a_row_outside_the_relay_window_is_parked_without_a_send` (asserts the sink saw no event at all), `open_parks_stale_rows_and_keeps_fresh_ones`, `enqueue_refuses_an_event_the_relay_cannot_accept`, `the_park_row_round_trips_through_the_ledger`, `only_a_final_relay_verdict_is_recognised_as_final`. 18/18 `publish::tests` green. **Not exercised against Brian's live provider or its real poisoned ledger**, and no installed build carries it yet.

### Process rules from the 2026-09-02 runs (keep)

- **One review pass per lane**, and the orchestrator reads the fix-round diff.
  Per-stage verification caught every real defect this day produced.
- **Prose is not evidence, for agents as for humans.** A gate is a command, an
  outcome and a tail, or it did not happen.
- A hotfix that blocks observation itself ships on fast gates with `just ci`
  after, disclosed; **everything else waits for `just ci`**.
- Never `pnpm install` in a tree whose `node_modules` is a symlink, and never
  `pnpm` at all in a `git archive` tree without the root lockfile (§3a).
- **Seats run the bundled `bee`**: relaunch the app after any CLI or provider
  landing, before the next live run.
